items.title: How AI & LLM Resume Screeners Rank Engineers in 2026: Vector Matching vs. Keyword ATS
items.pt:
Most software engineers still optimize their resumes for 2018-era literal string matching, stuffing exact acronyms into a bottom skills block while leaving their experience bullets vague. Meanwhile, 2026 hiring pipelines run a two-stage filter: a deterministic Applicant Tracking System (ATS) parser that extracts structured JSON fields, followed by an LLM or bi-encoder embedding ranker that scores semantic evidence, scope, and recency across your dated work history.

I build the parsing and scorin

items.title: Business analyst LinkedIn About section examples you can adapt
items.pt:
LinkedIn's own help page says the About section "should express your mission, motivation, and skills," and that you should ideally keep it to one or two paragraphs. items.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
items.pt: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. items.title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
items.pt: An estimator can be accurate and stable on typical data, yet sensitive to a few possible records. Differentially private mechanisms commonly scale their noise to the worst-case influence of a single record, which lets these records dictate the noise even when the remaining data would allow far less. items.pt: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. items.pt: Luggage re-identification (ReID) is a critical task in video surveillance for forensics, security or border management (suspicious or abandoned luggage recognition), as well as luggage management (lost luggage recovery).
